# zlaev2

> Computes the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaev2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlaev2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlaev2( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1 ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128` | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `b` | `Complex128` | (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `c` | `Complex128` | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |
| `cs1` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| `sn1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CS1, SN1) is a unit right eigenvector for RT1 |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) element and the conjugate of the (2,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.
- `sn1`: The vector (`CS1`, `SN1`) is a unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlaev2.strided( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1, offsetSn1 ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128` | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `b` | `Complex128` | (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `c` | `Complex128` | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |
| `cs1` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| `sn1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CS1, SN1) is a unit right eigenvector for RT1 |
| ↳ `offsetSn1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `sn1` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) element and the conjugate of the (2,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.
- `sn1`: The vector (`CS1`, `SN1`) is a unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlaev2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAEV2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlaev2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128 from '@stdlib/complex/float64/ctor/lib/index.js';
import zlaev2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlaev2';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';

const rt1 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt2 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const cs1 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const sn1 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const sn1v = reinterpret( sn1, 0 );

const a = new Complex128( 5.0, 0.0 );
const b = new Complex128( 1.0, 2.0 );
const c = new Complex128( 3.0, 0.0 );

zlaev2( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, cs1, sn1 );
console.log( 'rt1:', rt1[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'rt2:', rt2[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'cs1:', cs1[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'sn1:', sn1v[ 0 ], '+', sn1v[ 1 ], 'i' );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAEV2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAEV2 computes the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 Hermitian matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ \overline{B} & C \end{bmatrix}
$$

On return, `RT1` is the eigenvalue of larger absolute value, `RT2` is the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value, and (`CS1`,`SN1`) is the unit right eigenvector for `RT1`, giving the decomposition

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & \overline{\mathrm{SN1}} \\ -\mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ \overline{B} & C \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & -\overline{\mathrm{SN1}} \\ \mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{RT1} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{RT2} \end{bmatrix}
$$

### Further Details

`RT1` is accurate to a few ulps barring over/underflow.

`RT2` may be inaccurate if there is massive cancellation in the determinant $A \, C-B \, B$; higher precision or correctly rounded or correctly truncated arithmetic would be needed to compute `RT2` accurately in all cases.

`CS1` and `SN1` are accurate to a few ulps barring over/underflow.

Overflow is possible only if `RT1` is within a factor of 5 of overflow. Underflow is harmless if the input data is 0 or exceeds

underflow\_threshold / macheps.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
